But just as a side comment, as they evolved with Wi-Fi, they tried to make Wi-Fi more efficient. That means to reduce the overhead. And a way to reduce the overhead is to reduce the duration of these waiting times, like this or or the extended RFS or the slot time. It was twenty microseconds, now it's nine microseconds. So we reduced all these durations in order to make the protocol more efficient and reduce the overhead. As we said. Here, the expression is reported in a slightly different way, but it's exactly the same as before. But thanks to the fact that we have the contention window minimum that is now different for each access category, with the higher priority gap category that gets the smaller contention window minimum. Statistically, we have that the high priority traffic.
